title: Huaca Prieta early coastal occupation, Peru
summary: Excavation beneath the Huaca Prieta mound on Peru's north coast found remains of people who used the shore and nearby plants about 14,000 years ago. It is one of the early dated Pacific-coast sites in South America, thousands of years before the mound itself was built.

uncertainty.note: Range is the 14,200-13,300 calibrated years BP reported for the deep pre-mound levels (year = 1950 minus cal BP). A later study reports an intermittent presence from c. 15,000 years ago; that page was not opened here.

where.modern_name: Huaca Prieta, Chicama Valley, La Libertad Region, Peru
where.historical_name: Coast of what is now northern Peru; no polity at this date

importance.justification: A dated Late Pleistocene coastal occupation that informs how early Americans used marine resources.

sources.title: Late Pleistocene human presence at Huaca Prieta, Peru, and early Pacific Coastal adaptations
sources.author: Tom D. Dillehay and colleagues

reviewer_note: The record id says 15 ka; the opened pages give 14,200-13,300 cal BP (about 14,000 years ago), so the date follows them. The 2017 Science Advances paper (about 15,000 years) could not be opened (HTTP 403), so it is not cited. Pin is the mound site.
